method: For every plane and gate, identified the runtime subject, injected a representative defect, and asked whether the named test would fail. Then traced every dependency path and test ID to its current artifact/source.

resolves.B-OP-01: OPEN-BLOCKER: G5/G10/G11 are deliberation-artifact validators, not shipped-product release gates; the artifact answers two different release questions as one.
resolves.B-OP-02: OPEN-BLOCKER: the three gates counted as demonstrated can all pass while their advertised product properties are broken.
resolves.B-OP-03: OPEN-BLOCKER: ten unproved gates and an unmeasured non-blocking performance gate cannot constitute a release policy under the artifact's own anti-vacuity principle.
resolves.B-OP-04: OPEN-BLOCKER: G9 checks only identity equality, so a projection may omit or misstate verdict, Coverage, findings, termination, or truncation and still pass.
resolves.B-OP-05: OPEN-BLOCKER: per-Run budgets and mandatory ExecutionId correlation do not cover queries, mutations, pre-admission failures, or serve requests that create no Run.
resolves.B-OP-06: OPEN-BLOCKER: dependencies cite superseded threat-model.v1 and a non-existent no-flake source in architecture/09.
resolves.B-OP-07: OPEN-BLOCKER: G6 depends on PS-09/LN-11/LN-12 even though their artifacts admit no capability-denial mechanism and an unresolved closure boundary.
resolves.B-OP-08: OPEN-BLOCKER: no durable user-audit plane covers data inventory, excerpt access, export, purge, repair, and mutation receipts.
resolves.B-OP-09: OPEN-BLOCKER: G12 is made non-blocking because it has no pass condition; that records an unfinished decision rather than a safe release posture.

evidence: G5 invokes artifacts/check-d9.py, which validates the candidate JSON and a duplicate Python derivation, not the production process-boundary mapper
G10 invokes check-threat-claims.py over architecture prose/JSON
G11 invokes check-claims.py over this deliberation's status register
none executes a built opensip-cli artifact
findings.impact: A product release can pass all three 'demonstrated' gates without implementing the termination mapper, threat mitigations, or claim-status machinery at all.
findings.requiredChange: Separate architecture-artifact CI from product release gates. Keep the three checkers as design-integrity gates; add implementation conformance tests that invoke the built binary/library against the binding fixtures and mutation cases.
findings.confidence: high; verified by reading all three checker sources
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A production implementation imported/executed by those checkers. It currently is not.

evidence: check-threat-claims T2 only checks that primaryRisks is non-empty and T9 only checks that a gate label exists
its table skip misses architecture/05's unqualified Probe sandbox claim
check-claims passes the live METHOD.CLAIM-STATUS-INTEGRITY and stale-version/status contradictions in architecture/07 and /11
check-d9's derivation is implemented inside the checker rather than compared with the product mapper
findings.impact: The artifact violates its own principle that a gate able to pass while the protected property is broken is worse than no gate.
findings.requiredChange: Require a target implementation, an injected defect/negative control, and observed failure for every gate. Do not count a self-consistency validator as product conformance.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Recorded mutations against the actual implementation for G5/G10/G11.

findings.evidence: gateOnGates admits ten of thirteen gates have no failing case; OP-07 itself is only a sentence and no release-bootstrap rule says missing negative controls blocks release.
findings.impact: The artifact describes desired tests but cannot decide release readiness.
findings.requiredChange: Make gate qualification a prerequisite: a blocking gate is disabled/unqualified until its implementation target, positive case, negative mutation, and failure evidence are recorded. Product release is blocked while any required property lacks a qualified gate.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Executable negative controls and recorded catches for every blocking gate.

findings.evidence: G9 asserts only that every surface resolves the same Run and Finding identities.
findings.counterexample: JSON can carry the correct IDs but report verdict pass instead of fail; HTML can omit all Coverage; SARIF can silently truncate findings. G9 still passes.
findings.requiredChange: Define a per-surface semantic projection matrix over required fields and permitted loss. Golden-test verdict, termination, finding set/count, severity, Coverage/truncation, artifact availability, and Run/Finding identities from one canonical Run.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A normative projection schema elsewhere that G9 actually invokes.

evidence: volumeBudgets are per-Run
correlation requires ExecutionId on every event
architecture/07 and /08 define queries, mutations, serve requests, and pre-admission failures that do not create Runs and may not have an admitted ExecutionId
the command envelope already defines a command/request ID
findings.impact: Non-analysis diagnostics/progress are either unbudgeted or forced to mint analysis identities, breaking the command model.
findings.requiredChange: Use RequestId/CommandId on every event; add optional ExecutionId after attempt admission and optional RunId after seal. Budget by request/execution, with child budgets for stages and streams, not universally by Run.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A domain rule making every command an Execution without creating a Run, consistently reflected in D9 and the envelope.

evidence: TM.F3 and TM.PRIVACY cite superseded threat-model.v1 rather than v2
ARCH.NO-FLAKY cites architecture/09, but no flake policy appears anywhere in architecture/
the flake policy exists in repository guidance, not in this design's declared dependency
findings.impact: The artifact claims to discharge properties it did not inherit from an authoritative current source.
findings.requiredChange: Replace threat dependencies with v3 findings/properties and either add a greenfield no-flake decision artifact or mark the policy as an unreviewed proposal with its own rationale and status.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A resolvable architecture source containing the cited policy.

evidence: G6 asserts PS-09 and LN-11/LN-12
c2-plan-stage-schema.v2 knownLimitations says PS-09 assumes a runtime denial mechanism no artifact designs
r1-lifetime-neutrality v1.2 says LN-11's storage closure boundary is unresolved
both are conformance specifications, not implemented suites
findings.impact: A release-blocking capability gate has neither a defined enforcement boundary nor executable implementation.
findings.requiredChange: Design the enforcement mechanism and boundary first; split Rule capability denial, core ambient-authority closure, and host/process confinement into separate gates with target-specific negative controls.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: An implemented restricted runtime/build boundary that the tests attack through direct, transitive, dynamic, and injected paths.

evidence: Threat U6 requires knowing and undoing stored data
the four planes focus on analysis output/progress/diagnostics/telemetry
mutations, data inventory, excerpt retrieval, export, purge, and repair need durable user-auditable receipts but are not evidence of a code analysis verdict
findings.impact: Privacy-sensitive state changes can be neither reconstructed from ephemeral progress nor safely inserted into analysis evidence.
findings.requiredChange: Add or explicitly place a durable host-audit/mutation-receipt plane with RequestId, actor/client, project, privacy classes, before/after object commitments, and retention. Keep it out of the analysis EvidenceDigest while making it authoritative for the host mutation.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A normative mapping proving MutationReceipt and data-access events already inhabit one of the four planes with the required durability.

findings.evidence: G12 is non-blocking solely because no SLO or reference corpus has been defined, while the architecture makes agent-loop latency and bounded resources product-relevant.
findings.impact: Catastrophic performance/resource regressions can ship indefinitely; absence of a pass condition is used as a reason not to protect the property.
findings.requiredChange: Mark release policy incomplete until at least safety capacity limits (memory, disk, runtime/cancellation) and a reference capacity class exist. Product-latency SLO may remain product-owned, but resource-safety thresholds need a blocking gate before release.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: A separate release-readiness decision explicitly accepting unbounded performance risk for an initial experimental release.

accepted: evidence, progress, diagnostics, and telemetry have materially different authority/durability
telemetry and sinks must not influence verdicts
diagnostics and producer stderr need bounded privacy-aware handling
required: field-level privacy classification and budget-exhaustion semantics

sealedPropertiesCovered.assessment: Conceptually covered; OP-01 needs stronger sink-failure/config mutations.
A candidate JSON checker is not product termination conformance.
The artifact instead cites v1; privacy/offline gates are not discharged.
G11 relies on a mechanism whose own authoritative status is CANDIDATE and whose live false negatives are demonstrated.

knownLimitations: No implementation exists to execute product-level mutations against; this is exactly why the current release-gate status cannot be accepted.
This review does not choose numeric budgets or SLOs.
The four-plane taxonomy may be retained if mutation/audit receipts are normatively placed rather than added as a fifth plane.
whatWouldChangeOverallVerdict: A v2 separating design CI from product release gates, qualifying every blocker with implementation-level negative controls, strengthening projection parity, fixing identity/budget domains and dependencies, placing durable mutation audit, and defining minimum resource-safety release thresholds.
